verses.text: ¶ Paul a priſoner of Ieſus Chriſt, ⁊ Timothie our brother vnto Philemon our dearely beloued, and fellow labourer,
And to our beloued Apphia, and Archippus our fellow Souldier, and to the Church in thy houſe.
Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Ieſus Chriſt.
I thanke my God, making mention of thee alwayes in my prayers,
Hearing of thy loue, and faith, which thou haſt toward the Lord Ieſus, and toward all Saints:
That the communication of thy faith may become effectuall by the acknowledging of euery good thing, which is in you in Chriſt Ieſus.
For wee haue great ioy and conſolation in thy loue, becauſe the bowels of the Saints are refreſhed by thee, brother.
Wherefore, though I might bee much bolde in Chriſt to enioyne thee that which is conuenient;
Yet for loues ſake I rather beſeech thee, being ſuch a one as Paul the aged, and now alſo a priſoner of Ieſus Chriſt.
I beſeech thee for my ſonne Oneſimus, whome I haue begotten in my bonds,
Which in time paſt was to thee vnprofitable: but now profitable to thee and to me:
Whom I haue ſent againe: thou therfore receiue him, that is mine owne bowels.
Whome I would haue reteined with mee, that in thy ſtead hee might haue miniſtred vnto me in the bonds of the Goſpel.
But without thy minde would I doe nothing, that thy benefite ſhould not bee as it were of neceſſitie, but willingly.
For perhaps hee therefore departed for a ſeaſon, that thou ſhouldeſt receiue him for euer:
Not now as a ſeruant, but aboue a ſeruant, a brother beloued, ſpecially to mee, but how much more vnto thee, both in the fleſh, and in the Lord?
If thou count mee therefore a partner, receiue him as my ſelfe.
If hee hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account.
I Paul haue written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I doe not ſay to thee how thou oweſt vnto me, euen thine owne ſelfe beſides:
Yea, brother, let mee haue ioy of thee in the Lord: refreſh my bowles in the Lord.
Hauing confidence in thy obedience, I wrote vnto thee, knowing that thou wilt alſo doe more then I ſay.
But withall prepare mee alſo a lodging: for I truſt that through your prayers I ſhall be giuen vnto you.
There ſalute thee Epaphras, my fellow priſoner in Chriſt Ieſus:
Marcus, Ariſtarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellow labourers.
The grace of our Lord Ieſus Chriſt be with your ſpirit. Amen. ¶ Written from Rome to Philemon, by Oneſimus a ſeruant.
